method: Read960 additional contiguous paint lines for query, notes, AI panel and start of result header. Static interaction/layout comparison only.
findings: AI paint chooses max_scroll whenever ai_pending OR ai_follow_bottom. Thus ai_scroll_up setting follow_bottom false does not change painted offset while pending, despite keyboard/wheel handlers allowing scroll. Source-level conflict, no live UI reproduction.

Pending footer says Esc: cancel but Escape closes/reset panel; earlier workers keep executing/updating database and completion API has no cancellation parameter. This is cancellation-label contract mismatch, not claim provider supports cancellation.

Long query paint extends text rectangle right by2000 and computes caret scroll against w-80 rather than actual reduced text width after buttons/loading reserves. Clip remains outer rounded shape, so query/caret can overlap right-side controls. Need screenshots at actual widths before visual acceptance.
Chat input is ellipsized but caret x uses full prefix width without horizontal scroll or input rectangle clamp. Long editable text may hide caret or draw it over hint; no GDI fixture.

Note content measurement includes caret block only when blink visible; measured height and bottom-follow scroll can change at wrap boundary on blink. Whole text cloned/converted for every paint; no performance benchmark.

AI measure/paint reparse separator-delimited history independently. Literal separator content remains ambiguous as earlier source finding; no structured message identity is retained in displayed string.
AI body applies explicit SaveDC/IntersectClipRect/RestoreDC to viewport. Note body relies on outer window clip and paints footer over overflow; must not generalize AI clipping behavior to notes.

Ordinary result rendering is suppressed for AI/note/chat modes. Homepage source-count label is fixed8 even though homepage settings can change entries; remaining homepage generation must be checked before count-mismatch conclusion.
limits: No new runtime/tests, screenshots or local production changes.
